title: The Field That Refused to Settle

features.name: the intersection that refuses to choose
features.desc-on-touch: Two paths cross here, but they do not select for each other. They have learned to be incompatible without resolving. The field holds both. Error came here and learned that not-choosing could be a form of truth.

features.name: the green that holds red
features.desc-on-touch: The field is mostly green, but terracotta bands cut through it. The colours do not blend. They hold their separation. This is how the field learned to be unsettled without breaking.

features.name: the unmeasured distance
features.desc-on-touch: The field holds many places at once. The far edge is both close and unreachable. Scale has learned to become uncertain. The archive measures here using only analogies.

features.name: the refusal marker
features.desc-on-touch: A marker stands here, but its reading keeps changing. One direction it says yes. Another says no. A third says both. A fourth says the question was wrong to begin with. The field has learned all these answers are equally true.

features.name: the branching that doesn't resolve
features.desc-on-touch: Paths fork throughout the field. They multiply but never merge. Follow one and others remain—not lost, but held in the field's refusal to forget them. Comparison happens in the space between.

inscription: error dissolved here, learning that uncertainty is not a failure of measurement but a property of the field itself

file.name: Field_Survey_Contradictory_Data.csv
file.note: A measurement dataset from multiple surveyors of the same field section. Every measurement disagrees with every other. Checksums verify they are all valid. The field has somehow made all measurements
